Imagine starting your childhood surrounded not by comfort, but by barbed wire and suspicion. That’s where George Takei’s powerful memoir, They Called Us Enemy, takes us—right into the heart of Japanese American internment during World War II. Together, we’ll step into the shoes of a young boy whose family, like so many others, was suddenly uprooted from everything familiar and forced into camps by their own country.
Through every page, you’ll feel the confusion, the resilience, and the quiet determination it takes to hold onto dignity when the world feels turned upside down. What does it mean to belong, or to stay loyal, when everything you know is questioned? In the daily routines of camp life, families do their best to cling to hope and humanity, even when the future is so uncertain.
As we journey through these memories, we’ll see just how complicated patriotism and prejudice can be—how fear and misunderstanding can tear communities apart and shape lives in ways that last for generations. George Takei’s story invites us not just to look back, but to really feel what it’s like to face injustice and to see how family bonds and the fight for justice can light the way forward.
So, let’s explore this moving story together. Along the way, we’ll uncover lessons about courage, compassion, and the power of remembering—lessons that still matter, maybe more than ever, today.
